clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk. NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and may increase warfarin levels through protein binding displacement.
management: Avoid combination. Use acetaminophen for pain if possible. If NSAID required, monitor INR closely.

clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk. NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and may displace warfarin from protein binding sites.
management: Avoid combination. Use acetaminophen for pain if possible.

clinical_effect: Potential increased bleeding risk. COX-2 inhibitors have less platelet effect but can still increase INR.
management: Monitor INR closely if combination necessary. Consider dose reduction of warfarin.

clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk through platelet inhibition and potential warfarin displacement.
management: Avoid combination. Use acetaminophen instead.

clinical_effect: Macrolide antibiotics may increase warfarin effect by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and altering gut flora vitamin K production.
management: Monitor INR within 3-5 days of starting azithromycin. May need warfarin dose adjustment.

clinical_effect: Fluoroquinolones inhibit CYP1A2 metabolism of warfarin, significantly increasing INR and bleeding risk.
management: If combination necessary, reduce warfarin dose by 25-50% and monitor INR every 2-3 days.

description: Oxycodone + Alprazolam interaction (FDA Black Box Warning)
clinical_effect: Concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine use increases risk of respiratory depression, profound sedation, coma, and death.
management: FDA black box warning. Avoid combination unless no alternative exists. If combined, use lowest effective doses and shortest duration.

clinical_effect: Concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine use increases risk of respiratory depression, profound sedation, coma, and death.
management: FDA black box warning. Avoid combination unless no alternative exists.

management: FDA black box warning. Avoid combination.

description: Fentanyl + Alprazolam interaction (FDA Black Box Warning)
clinical_effect: Concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine use — highest risk combination. Fentanyl potency makes respiratory depression particularly dangerous.
management: FDA black box warning. Avoid combination. If unavoidable, extreme caution with monitoring.

clinical_effect: Serotonin syndrome risk. Both drugs increase serotonergic activity. Also increased seizure risk with tramadol.
management: Avoid combination if possible. If used together, monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms.

clinical_effect: High serotonin syndrome risk. Both drugs significantly increase serotonin. Also increased seizure threshold lowering.
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative analgesic.

clinical_effect: Hyperkalemia risk. ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone-mediated potassium excretion. Adding potassium-sparing diuretic compounds this effect.
management: If combination necessary, monitor serum potassium within 1 week and regularly thereafter. Avoid in patients with eGFR < 30.

clinical_effect: Hyperkalemia risk. ARBs reduce aldosterone-mediated potassium excretion similar to ACE inhibitors.
management: Monitor serum potassium closely. Avoid if potassium already elevated.

clinical_effect: Dual RAAS blockade increases risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, and renal failure without proven mortality benefit.
management: Avoid combination. Use one RAAS agent only.

clinical_effect: Serotonin syndrome risk from dual serotonergic therapy. No clinical benefit from combining two SSRIs.
management: Never combine two SSRIs. Cross-taper if switching between agents.

clinical_effect: Serotonin syndrome risk. Duplicate serotonergic mechanism with no added benefit.
management: Never combine. Use one SSRI at a time.

clinical_effect: Serotonin syndrome risk. Overlapping serotonergic mechanisms increase toxicity risk.
management: Avoid combination. Cross-taper with washout period if switching.

clinical_effect: Macrolide antibiotics inhibit CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin levels and risk of rhabdomyolysis.
management: Suspend simvastatin during macrolide course. Or use pravastatin (not CYP3A4 metabolized).

clinical_effect: Diltiazem inhibits CYP3A4, significantly increasing simvastatin levels. Risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
management: Simvastatin dose should not exceed 10mg/day with diltiazem. Consider switching to pravastatin or rosuvastatin.

clinical_effect: Amiodarone increases digoxin levels by 70-100% by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and reducing renal clearance.
management: Reduce digoxin dose by 50% when initiating amiodarone. Monitor digoxin levels closely.

clinical_effect: Thiazide-induced hypokalemia increases sensitivity to digoxin toxicity.
management: Monitor potassium levels. Consider potassium supplementation or potassium-sparing agent.

clinical_effect: NSAIDs reduce antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and may worsen renal function.
management: Monitor blood pressure and renal function. Use lowest NSAID dose for shortest duration.

clinical_effect: NSAIDs reduce antihypertensive effect of ARBs and may worsen renal function.
management: Monitor blood pressure and renal function. Limit NSAID use.

clinical_effect: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk when combined with direct oral anticoagulants.
management: Avoid combination. If NSAID needed, use lowest dose for shortest time and monitor for bleeding.

clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk combining DOAC with NSAID.
management: Avoid combination. Use acetaminophen for pain management.

clinical_effect: Fluoroquinolones can cause unpredictable blood glucose changes (both hypo- and hyperglycemia) when combined with antidiabetics.
management: Monitor blood glucose closely during antibiotic course.

clinical_effect: Beta-blockers may reduce bronchodilator effect of albuterol. Metoprolol (beta-1 selective) less likely but possible at higher doses.
management: Use cardioselective beta-blocker at lowest effective dose. Monitor respiratory function.

clinical_effect: Combined CNS depression. Gabapentin can potentiate opioid-related respiratory depression.
management: FDA warning. Use lowest effective doses. Monitor for respiratory depression.

clinical_effect: Combined CNS depression with increased respiratory depression risk.
management: FDA warning. Use with caution at lowest doses.

clinical_effect: Serotonin syndrome risk and increased seizure risk.
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative analgesic.

clinical_effect: High-dose acetaminophen (>2g/day for >3 days) may increase INR modestly.
management: Preferred over NSAIDs with warfarin. Keep dose under 2g/day if possible. Monitor INR.

clinical_effect: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 metabolism of warfarin, increasing INR by 50-70%.
management: Reduce warfarin dose by 30-50% when starting amiodarone. Monitor INR weekly for first month.

clinical_effect: PPIs may slightly increase apixaban exposure, though clinical significance is debated.
management: Generally safe. Monitor if high PPI doses used long-term.

clinical_effect: Serotonin syndrome risk. Also fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, increasing duloxetine levels.
management: Avoid combination. Note fluoxetine has very long half-life requiring extended washout.

clinical_effect: Additive negative chronotropic and inotropic effects. Risk of severe bradycardia, AV block, and heart failure.
management: Avoid combination. If needed, use with extreme caution and cardiac monitoring.

clinical_effect: No clinical benefit from combining benzodiazepines. Additive CNS depression, respiratory depression, falls risk.
management: Never combine two benzodiazepines. Use one agent at appropriate dose.
